articles.title: Over 50% Indian women of reproductive age are anaemic: ICMR
articles.summary: Over 50 per cent of Indian women aged 15 to 49 are anaemic, according to the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) by the Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN). Instead of conventional finger-prick testing, venous blood testing was used in the SAMPADA survey , since it is the gold standard approach for measuring and classifying anaemia and its underlying nutritional causes in population-level public health surveys. Anaemia has remained a controversial health condition in India, with the debate centred on how the condition was measured. In 2023, the Ministry of Health dropped anaemia testing from the National Family Health Survey-6 (NFHS-6) due to concerns over the accuracy of the finger-prick blood sampling method. It was argued that it could potentially overstate anaemia prevalence. Therefore, this survey had been much-awaited to understand the current prevalence of anaemia in the Indian population. The statistics revealed that 55.9 per cent of the surveyed women aged 15 to 49 are anaemic. Around 26 per cent of women are mildly anaemic, 26.9 per cent are moderately anaemic, and 2.9 per cent severely anaemic. Dr Rajiv Bahl, secretary, department of health research and director general, ICMR, said, "It is encouraging that the prevalence of anaemia is lower in SAMPADA compared to previous national surveys. The comprehensive anaemia profiling in the SAMPADA survey provides an evidence base to strengthen the ongoing national efforts towards Anaemia Mukt Bharat." The NFHS-5 , conducted in 2019-21, showed that 57 per cent of the women aged 15 to 49 were anaemic. However, the parameters of comparison are different in the survey and cannot be compared to the latest one. Therefore, the new estimates cannot be interpreted as an overall improvement. Especially since the data on anaemic women in the age group of 15 to 49 differs by just one per cent. Will Health Minister Nadda survive release of 'damning report' on anaemia prevalence: Congress Meanwhile, the survey also present some interesting findings. The assessment of micronutrient deficiencies has revealed that anaemia is not caused by iron deficiency alone. While 55.9 per cent of women of reproductive age (WRA) are anaemic, only 26.7 per cent have coexisting iron deficiency and anaemia. Among adolescent girls, 46.3 per cent are anaemic, while 26.9 per cent have iron-deficiency anaemia. This implies that iron supplements are not sufficient to control anaemia. However, the patterns of Vitamin B12 deficiency are different. Nearly 40 to 60 per cent of people across all age groups are deficient, peaking in adolescents (65.4 per cent in girls, 66.1 per cent in boys), pregnant women (63.1 per cent), and adult men (60.4 per cent). Notably, B12 deficiency rates are nearly identical in both anaemic and non-anaemic individuals. Folate deficiency also remains low nationwide affecting only 9.8 per cent of the surveyed population. It ranged nearly 2.9 per cent in pregnant women, and 10.2 per cent in children aged 5 to 9 years.

articles.title: Explained: India-UK Scotch whisky classification issue
articles.summary: New Delhi: India and the UK implemented a trade agreement on July 15, 2026. Under the pact, both sides reduced or eliminated customs/import duties on the maximum number of goods traded between them. India reduced import duties on Scotch whisky , meeting a key demand of the UK under the India-UK CETA (comprehensive economic and trade agreement). Importers initially availed the concessional duty rates after the agreement came into force on July 15, but an issue recently emerged over allegations that some importers were claiming the benefits under different HS code classifications. Here is an explainer of different terminologies to understand the matter. India to charge bulk Scotch imports 162.5% duty and tax amid UK pact standoff India's Scotch probe of Diageo, Pernod undermining India-UK pact benefits, trade group says HS Code A product traded between two countries is identified under a standard product classification system. It is called as the Harmonised Commodity Description and Coding System, or simply the Harmonised System (HS). It's an internationally recognised identification number given to a product for international trade. For example, whisky, tea, mobile phones, and steel all have particular HS classifications. It ensures that customs authorities in different countries identify products using a common code. World Customs Organisation Developed and maintained by the Brussels-based World Customs Organization (WCO), HS Code system was introduced in 1988 and is used by over 200 countries for customs tariffs and international trade statistics. It is periodically updated to reflect changes in technology, products and global trade. HS Codes Structure It starts with a six-digit code, which is divided into three levels. The first two digits represent the Chapter, which indicates the broad category of goods. The first four digits form the Heading, identifying a more specific product group. The first six digits constitute the Subheading, providing a more detailed classification of the product. Countries can add further digits to these six-digit international codes for their own customs and trade requirements. India uses an eight-digit ITC (Indian Trade Classification)-HS classification for customs and trade purposes. Example: Take alcoholic beverages. Chapter 22 covers beverages, spirits and vinegar. Heading 2208 covers undenatured ethyl alcohol of an alcoholic strength by volume of less than 80 per cent, spirits, liqueurs and other spirituous beverages. Subheading 220830 specifically covers whiskies. Eight-digit: 2208 3012 covers Scotch whisky (specifically in containers holding 2 litres or less); 2208 3013 classifies blended whisky (in containers holding 2 litres or less); and 2208 3092 (bulk). India's eight-digit tariff codes further distinguish between different types of whisky. This distinction is important because two products that appear commercially similar may fall under different customs classifications. India will honour duty cuts on Scotch imports from UK India to meet liquor firms as domestic giants join foreign peers in Scotch dispute Importance of HS Codes They are not merely identification numbers, as they determine several important aspects of international trade. Customs duty: Every product classification has a prescribed customs duty. If a product is classified under a different heading, the applicable import duty can change. FTA benefits: The agreements provide preferential duty rates for specified products under specified tariff lines. Trade statistics: Governments use HS codes to calculate imports, exports, trade deficits and sector-wise trade performance. Regulatory requirements: Product classifications help determine whether particular licences, restrictions, standards or other regulatory requirements apply. Trade disputes: Differences over classification can lead to disagreements between importers and customs authorities, sometimes resulting in litigation. In short, the classification of a product can directly affect the cost of importing it and the benefits available under a trade agreement. India-UK Trade Pact Issue: Chapter 22 and Whiskey Classification Chapter 22 of the Customs Tariff covers beverages, spirits and vinegar. It has several headings for different categories of alcoholic products. Under HS heading 2207, the classification covers undenatured ethyl alcohol and denatured spirits. Heading 2208 covers spirits, liqueurs and other spirituous beverages. Its subheadings include 220810 for compound alcoholic preparations used in the manufacture of beverages, 220820 for brandy, 220830 for whisky, 220840 for rum, 220850 for gin, 220860 for vodka, and 220870 for liqueurs and cordials. Another code in the picture is 21069051. It covers "compound alcoholic preparations of a kind used for the manufacture of beverages". One important point: the Indian tariff has eight-digit codes, which provide more detailed classifications than the six-digit international HS system. For example, under heading 220830, India has separate tariff items for Scotch, blended whisky, bourbon and other whiskies. The present India-UK issue revolves around the classification of certain bulk Scotch whisky imports and whether they qualify for the preferential duty offered under the trade agreement. Bulk and Bottled Scotch Whisky Bottled is the finished product, packed in bottles and ready for sale to consumers. It is imported by companies for direct distribution and retail sale in India. Examples include Johnnie Walker (Red Label, Black Label, Gold Label Reserve, Blue Label), Chivas Regal, Dewar's, Glenfiddich, and The Glenlivet. Bulk, on the other hand, is imported in large containers, barrels or casks rather than retail bottles. It is generally brought into India for further processing, blending, dilution and bottling by domestic manufacturers. It can arrive at a higher alcohol concentration, often around 58-63 per cent alcohol by volume (ABV), compared with the lower strength at which whisky is generally bottled for retail sale. ABV is the percentage of a liquid beverage that consists of pure ethanol (alcohol), measured at 20°C. A higher ABV percentage means a stronger drink. Indian liquor manufacturers use imported Scotch spirit as an input in their manufacturing operations. They may add water to bring down the alcohol strength and bottle it, or use it as a component in blended whisky products. This is where the classification issue begins. According to experts, should the product be classified according to what it actually is when it arrives in India, namely Scotch whisky, or according to its intended further use as an input for manufacturing alcoholic beverages?. Importers argue that the liquid is already Scotch whisky when it enters India. Its bulk packaging and subsequent dilution or bottling should not change its basic identity. The Customs authorities have questioned whether certain high-strength concentrates or compound alcoholic preparations should instead be treated as industrial inputs used to manufacture beverages. The distinction has a direct impact on customs duty. India-UK CETA and Scotch Before the agreement, the aggregate effective customs duty on eligible Scotch whisky imports was 150 per cent plus local levies. Under the pact, the duty was reduced to 75 per cent when the pact came into force. It is scheduled to decline further to 40 per cent over the next 10 years for products under 220830. And for 220890, the duty was reduced to 110 per cent. The 21069051 code is not part of the pact, so it attracts MFN (most favoured nation) tariff of 150 per cent plus other reliefs. The figures clearly show that different tariff classifications are treated differently and should not be treated as interchangeable. The Issue Bottled Scotch whisky under HS 22083012 and HS 22083013 is being imported as per the preferential duty offered under CETA. The present issue concerns only the customs classification of certain bulk, high-strength spirit imported from the UK for dilution, blending and bottling in India. This situation has arisen due to the fact that the said products have been imported under different HS codes in the past. For many years, major importers declared most of these goods, described as Compound Alcoholic Preparations (CAP), Concentrates of Alcoholic Beverages (CAB) or bulk whisky (raw material), under sub-heading 2208 90. The importers' own stand before Indian courts, over decades, has been that such bulk spirit is a raw material and not whisky. This practice seems to be in the knowledge of the UK Scotch Whisky Association, as is borne out by their submissions to the House of Commons Business and Trade Committee. The Association has stated that this tariff line was being used for the majority of bulk Scotch whisky exports for regulatory reasons, but had not been liberalised to the same extent as the Scotch-specific tariff lines. The House of Commons Business and Trade Committee, in its report on the CETA published on 21.01.2026, has recorded the concerns raised by the Scotch Whisky Association regarding tariff liberalisation under HS 2208 90. The matter, therefore, is about classifying the goods under the correct tariff line and applying the corresponding duty. The Government of India remains fully committed to the India-UK CETA. The Department of Commerce is working with the Department of Revenue, the industry and the UK side for an early resolution of the matter. Seized Consignments The commerce ministry has urged the DRI to release all the bulk Scotch consignments after following due process, until a technical solution is found to the issue. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal Agarwal said: "The genesis of this import under 220890 has to do with some legal judgements in the past wherein the importing industry has gone to the court and said that we want to import under 220890 and not 220830. The Revenue Department was of the view that it can be imported under 220830. But importing companies went to court. In 1991, there was a judgment and in 2004, the case went to the Supreme Court. So a lot of imports were happening under 220890...And these two tariff lines have got different levels of concessions". "So the technical point is that what (duty) should we be applying? Where should we land, actually and how should it be done? Because we don't want to get into some amendment... While negotiating probably, negotiators were not aware that what was coming to 220890 also was called Scotch whisky. We are working with the Ministry of Finance to find a technical solution. Finding a technical solution also requires that we don't go against the Honourable Court's order as such. But definitely the concessions under CETA also are to be equally respected. So we are working very closely. We have written to them; we have talked to them."

The move follows investigations into the September incident in Banda, which revealed that while the victims had consumed alcohol, they were already suffering from serious liver and kidney ailments, they said. Keeping this in mind, District Magistrate Dilip Kumar Yadav launched the drive through a joint team of the Health and Excise departments to screen regular drinkers and advise them to abstain from alcohol, an official said. Chief Medical and Health Officer (CMHO) Devesh Pateriya said the drive was aimed at raising awareness among drinkers about the direct impact of alcohol on their health. "In recent times, there have been several cases of alcohol-related deaths. Pateriya said individuals were being specifically screened for liver and kidney function, informed of their health status and advised to undergo periodic check-ups and quit alcohol. Even those who reported no immediate symptoms were cautioned that health complications could surface later, he added. Excise Inspector Shailendra Singh said probes into several recent alcohol-linked deaths in the district showed that pre-existing liver and kidney illnesses were the primary cause of death. articles.title: Centre tells SC it has limited scope to secure return of man serving in Russian Army as he has renounced Indian citizenship
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Centre has told the Supreme Court that its ability to secure the return of an Indian-origin man, who has acquired Russian nationality and is serving in the Army there, was limited. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, on Monday, was hearing a petition of a person seeking a direction to the Centre to bring back his son fighting in the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, said that the man had reportedly renounced his Indian citizenship and acquired Russian nationality before joining the Russian armed forces and, consequently, the government may have a very limited role in this. Man 'detained' in Russia, pressured to join war, alleges family; 2nd such case in Chhattisgarh The top law officer, taking note of the observation of the bench, said the government would explore possible avenues for the man's repatriation, including the scope for humanitarian intervention. However, he maintained that Russian authorities were within their rights to withhold information about him, given that he was now enrolled in their military as a Russian citizen. The bench was hearing a petition filed by the man's father and asked the Union government to explore all possible options to facilitate his return to India. Several aspects of the case remained unclear, particularly the agreement that he had entered into with the intermediary who had arranged his studies in Moscow, the bench said. The court also sought to know whether the Centre could intervene after Russian authorities informed Indian officials that the man had relinquished his Indian citizenship and obtained Russian nationality. Responding to the court's queries, Mehta said he would seek instructions from the ministry concerned on the possibility of extending humanitarian assistance in the matter. According to the petitioner's account, his son had travelled to Russia in April to pursue his studies. However, months after his departure, his family received a communication from the Indian Embassy in Moscow indicating that he had joined the Russian Army as a Russian citizen. Husband trapped in Russia-Ukraine war zone, Telangana woman's endless wait to tell him he is a father again In its communication to the family, the Embassy said it had taken up the matter with Russia's Ministry of Defence and requested his release. It further stated that, according to documents available with it, the man had voluntarily relinquished his Indian citizenship and possessed a Russian passport. The Embassy also informed the family that it would provide further updates once it received a response from the Russian authorities. The father, in his plea, expressed serious concern over the circumstances in which the man had reportedly acquired Russian citizenship and subsequently entered military service within a relatively short period of arriving in the country. The petitioner has raised questions about the circumstances surrounding the change in his son's citizenship status and his subsequent recruitment into the Russian armed forces, seeking the Centre's intervention to facilitate his return.

articles.title: The New Security Blueprint for Jewellery Retailers: Integrating Physical Protection, Technology and Risk Management
articles.summary: For India’s jewellery industry, security has always been fundamental to business. What is changing is the nature of the risks and the approach required to address them. With gold prices remaining elevated and jewellery retailers expanding across metropolitan centres and emerging Tier-II and Tier-III markets, the value concentrated in showrooms, warehouses and supply chains continues to grow. As retail operations expand, traditional security practices must evolve to meet the demands of a more complex business environment. Security can no longer be viewed as simply installing a safe or monitoring a showroom. Jewellery inventory moves continuously between display counters, storage facilities, workshops and multiple retail locations, creating several points of potential exposure. Employees, managers, security personnel and logistics partners may all interact with different parts of this process. Consequently, risks arise not only from external intrusion but also from unauthorised access, procedural lapses and human error. Protecting high-value assets therefore requires a broader understanding of how security operates across the entire retail network. Physical Protection Remains the Foundation With the security landscape evolving across physical as well as digital domains, physical protection remains indispensable. Certified fire- and burglary-resistant safes, high-security vaults, modular strongrooms and vault doors continue to play a critical role in resisting attacks and delaying unauthorised entry, allowing time for detection and response. However, as retail networks expand, security infrastructure must be aligned with the specific requirements of each location. A flagship showroom, a central warehouse and an outlet in an emerging market may have different operational needs and risk profiles. Retailers must therefore look beyond standardised solutions and assess the level of protection required for their assets and operating environments. Technology Is Changing the Way Security Works The evolution of physical security is increasingly being shaped by technology. Electronic locking systems, biometric authentication, dual-control mechanisms, time-delay functions and digital audit trails can strengthen access management and improve accountability. Knowing that a vault has been opened is useful; understanding who accessed it, when the access occurred, and whether it was authorised provides a more complete picture of potential risk. Surveillance systems are evolving in a similar direction. Intelligent video analytics and computer vision can help identify unusual activity, while connected alarms and access-control systems support faster responses to potential threats. These capabilities give retailers greater visibility into security events and help them make more informed decisions. Technology, however, does not diminish the importance of physical safeguards or established operating procedures. Advanced surveillance cannot compensate for inadequate storage protection, just as sophisticated access controls cannot replace disciplined management of permissions. The real value of technology lies in strengthening existing security measures and making them more responsive to changing operational needs. Managing Risk Across a Growing Retail Network Expansion brings its own set of security challenges. As retailers move from a handful of outlets to larger, geographically dispersed networks, differences in infrastructure, staffing capabilities, and local risk conditions become increasingly significant. Applying identical security measures across every location may not adequately address these variations. A more effective approach combines consistent organisational standards with location-specific risk assessments. This includes reviewing access permissions, managing keys and credentials, establishing clear alarm-response procedures, and ensuring that security remains effective during power outages or connectivity failures. Regular assessments also help businesses identify emerging vulnerabilities and adapt their measures as operations evolve. Security must therefore be treated as an ongoing management responsibility rather than a periodic compliance exercise. The effectiveness of any system depends not only on the infrastructure installed but also on the people, processes and response mechanisms supporting it. Building Security for the Future For jewellery retailers, the priority is to ensure that physical protection, technology and operational procedures work in alignment with the risks the business faces. Procurement decisions must look beyond product features to consider certified performance with specific focus on burglary or fire resistance, operational suitability and the ability to maintain effective protection as the business grows. Ultimately, the changing jewellery retail landscape calls for a shift in perspective. Traditional security measures remain essential, but their effectiveness increasingly depends on how well they are supported by technology, sound procedures and continuous risk assessment. The objective is not to replace established security practices, but to strengthen them for the realities of modern retail. articles.title: Karnataka Chief Minister tours Japan’s Maishima incineration plant, explores waste-to-energy models
articles.summary: Bengaluru: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and his delegation visited the Maishima Incineration Plant in Osaka, Japan, on Tuesday to study waste-to-energy technology and explore sustainable urban waste management solutions, officials said. Located on Maishima Island, the facility has been operational since 2001 and processes up to 900 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily through two incinerators, they said. "Designed by renowned Austrian artist Friedensreich Hundertwasser, the facility features a colourful façade, unconventional architectural forms and extensive greenery. The design brings together art, ecology and industrial infrastructure, demonstrating how essential urban facilities can also serve as spaces for environmental awareness," the CMO said. The visit is part of Karnataka's efforts to study and adopt internationally established models in urban planning, infrastructure and environmental management, officials said. The state government aims to draw lessons from such facilities to strengthen urban infrastructure, promote scientific and efficient waste disposal, explore waste-to-energy solutions and develop cleaner, more sustainable and liveable cities, they said. Earlier in the day, Shivakumar travelled from Nagoya to Osaka on Japan's Shinkansen bullet train and interacted with Kannadigas and their families at the station, the CMO said. The interaction provided an opportunity to connect with members of the Kannada community, exchange greetings and hear about their experiences of living in Japan, it said. The journey also offered an opportunity to observe Japan's organised Shinkansen network, connectivity and transport infrastructure, which could provide insights for Karnataka's efforts to strengthen urban mobility and public transport systems, officials added.

articles.summary: Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav reviewed the action plans prepared by the Urban Development and Housing Department and the Panchayat & Rural Development Department for water management and the existing water supply arrangements in all urban local bodies and rural areas of the state on Monday. Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said that water is essential for everyone, whether human beings or livestock. Therefore, every possible measure must be taken to ensure an adequate water supply for all. He directed officials to make the best possible use of available water resources to ensure that everyone gets access to water. The Chief Minister said that areas with adequate water availability must receive an uninterrupted supply, while long-term and sustainable solutions should be developed for water-deficient areas. He also directed that additional arrangements, including water supply through tankers, tube-well drilling and water harvesting, be developed in areas facing water shortages. If necessary, restrictive measures should also be taken to conserve water. He directed the Collectors to prepare separate action plans for effective water management and drinking water supply in urban and rural areas of their respective districts. The Chief Minister also instructed them to further strengthen group water supply schemes. Permission for new tube-well drilling would be granted wherever required. The Collectors were asked to pay special attention to rural areas, along with urban centres, and ensure adequate water supply. Necessary instructions have also been issued to urban local bodies to ensure adequate drinking water supply until June 30, 2027. The urban local bodies (ULBs) have been directed to use their own water sources, acquired water sources and their tankers as the first option for transporting water if a crisis arises despite the combined efforts of all departments. She further informed that nearly one lakh works related to water management and drinking water supply are currently in progress across the state. articles.title: 'Chor hai tera chacha': Priyanka Gandhi slapped boy who teased her in school after Emergency
articles.summary: New Delhi: Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said she slapped a boy in school after he teased her following the Emergency, saying, " Chor hai tera chacha (Your uncle is a thief)". She narrated the incident during a conversation with her mother Sonia Gandhi and her brother Rahul Gandhi, a video of which was shared by them on social media platforms on Tuesday. "After the Emergency, when dadi (Indira Gandhi) lost the election, we moved to a different house. I remember there was a lot of tension," Priyanka Gandhi says in the video. 'Felt the pull of power': Sonia Gandhi recalls decision not to become PM in 2004 Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi reminisce about their first day at school after Indira Gandhi lost the election in 1977. "I remember a little boy coming and telling me, ' Tera chacha (Sanjay Gandhi) jail mein hai, chor hai tera chacha '. So I slapped him; he started crying and went to the teacher, and I got a scolding," Priyanka Gandhi recalls in the video of her conversation with her mother and brother. Rahul Gandhi says he and his sister were different in school. The siblings playfully tease each other in the video, with Priyanka Gandhi recalling that she was a prefect in school. "There was a difference because she (Priyanka) was not rebellious. She would follow the rules; she would be sweet and nice, and I was rebellious and asking questions and disturbing," Rahul Gandhi recalls. Priyanka Gandhi then says she was suited to the system, unlike Rahul. "Even today, like in Parliament, it is the same difference that was there in class that we used to have. I would say 'good morning, namaste'. You were on your own trip," Priyanka Gandhi tells her brother. Rahul Gandhi also remembers that when he arrived at school after the Emergency, no one sat next to him. ‘I tried hard to belong, was terrified of mother-in-law’: Sonia Gandhi recalls life with Rajiv at memoir launch He also says that on his seventh birthday, none of his friends turned up, barring one, who is still his friend. In the video shared days after the launch of Sonia Gandhi's memoir ' Belonging: A Journey Of Love ', the three are seen reminiscing about moments of joy, laughter and pain they felt at various points of their lives. From dominating headlines since its announcement in August to flying off bookstore shelves, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir has had a blockbuster run, with HarperCollins India CEO Ananth Padmanabhan saying last week that it has sold "over two lakh copies" in less than a week, broken multiple publishing records and emerged as one of the "biggest memoirs" in independent India's history. ' Belonging: A Journey of Love ’ was officially launched at a packed event at ITC Maurya here last week, attended by the who's who of the Congress and the INDIA bloc, literary figures and a host of chief ministers, including Tamil Nadu's C Joseph Vijay. Describing her brother-in-law Sanjay Gandhi as a "man in a hurry", Congress leader Sonia Gandhi says in the book he had a "significant role" in decision-making during the Emergency despite lacking a constitutional locus standi for some of his political interventions. Deep down, then prime minister Indira Gandhi had never been entirely at ease with the Emergency but felt compelled by the "prevailing havoc of the time", Sonia Gandhi, who had an inside view of the goings-on during the June 1975 to March 1977 period, writes in her memoir. articles.title: Preparation for Clean and Green Simhastha 2028
articles.summary: Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav has said that there must be no shortcomings in the management of Simhastha 2028, the world's largest religious congregation. All preparations should be completed well in advance. He directed that all ongoing and approved works related to Simhastha arrangements must be completed by the end of 2027 under all circumstances. He also instructed that permanent access roads be constructed to connect all ghats along the Kshipra River. Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said that meetings of the Cabinet Committee on Simhastha would now be held every month to review ongoing and proposed works. He emphasised that this edition of Simhastha should be organised under the theme of ‘Clean and Green Simhastha’. Chief Minister Dr. Yadav was addressing the seventh meeting of the Cabinet Committee constituted to approve and monitor arrangements for Simhastha 2028 at the Mantralaya on Monday. The committee approved 33 proposed works worth Rs. 2,801.75 crore, as recommended by the Supervisory Committee. Special Focus on Power Supply, Sanitation, Security, Transport and Healthcare To expedite preparations for Simhastha Mahakumbh, 33 works recommended by the Supervisory Committee at its ninth and tenth meetings were placed before the Cabinet Committee for approval. These works have an estimated cost of Rs. 2,801.75 crore, comprising 16 works worth Rs. 1,457.04 crore recommended at the ninth meeting and 17 works worth Rs. 1,344.71 crore recommended at the tenth meeting. The proposed works cover temporary infrastructure, electricity, sanitation, healthcare, fire safety, traffic management, accommodation and security arrangements in the Mela area. These initiatives aim to ensure a safe, convenient and well-organised experience for the millions of devotees expected from across the country and abroad. Rs. 387.99 Cr Action Plan for Uninterrupted Power Supply The Energy Department presented a temporary action plan worth Rs. 387.99 crore to ensure uninterrupted power supply and alternative distribution arrangements across the Mela area, ghats and major roads during Simhastha 2028. The plan includes five temporary 33/11 kV substations, 45 km of 33 kV lines, 200 km of 11 kV lines, 550 km of LT lines and approximately 1,000 distribution transformer structures. Around 4,500 electricity connections will be provided to camps and institutions of saints and seers. To ensure uninterrupted lighting during emergencies, the plan proposes deploying 250 generators and 250 mobile light towers, along with 260 Ring Main Units (RMUs) and 1,000 automatic changeover switches. In addition, the Ujjain Municipal Corporation will spend Rs. 113.03 crore on temporary street lighting, high-mast and mini-mast lights, and decorative illumination across the city and Mela area. Major Investment in Sanitation and Cleanliness Under the commitment to organise a Clean Simhastha, the Ujjain Municipal Corporation has proposed Rs. 393.53 crore for the construction, operation and maintenance of toilets, urinals and bathing facilities. Across the approximately 2,584-hectare Mela area, a total of 8,169 sanitation complexes comprising 1,74,858 units have been proposed. These will include approximately 1.19 lakh toilets, 23,200 bathing facilities and 31,600 urinals. Public toilets will be available at intervals of approximately 500 metres. For women devotees, 185 changing-room complexes will be constructed along the ghats at intervals of approximately 200 metres. Of these, 85 complexes are proposed to be provided through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives. An additional plan worth Rs. 153.73 crore has been proposed for solid waste collection and transportation, cleanliness and vector control. During the major bathing days, approximately 2,500 tonnes of waste are expected to be generated daily. To ensure effective sanitation management, 13,000 sanitation workers will be deployed daily, with their activities monitored through GPS and an Integrated Command and Control Centre. Measures will also be taken to prevent diseases such as malaria, dengue, chikungunya and cholera. To improve the water quality of the Kshipra River, in-situ treatment, bioremediation and real-time water quality monitoring have been proposed at a cost of Rs. 12.33 crore. The Dewas Municipal Corporation has also proposed a project worth Rs. 1.50 crore to construct an intake well on the Nagdhammana River and connect contaminated water to the existing Sewage Treatment Plant (STP), ensuring clean water for devotees taking ritual baths. Healthcare, Fire Safety and Disaster Management The Public Health and Medical Education Department has proposed Rs. 27.78 crore for medical services during Simhastha, covering medicines, equipment, control rooms and first-aid training. An allocation of Rs. 18.23 crore has been proposed for fire services, while a proposal worth Rs. 155.08 crore for Home Guards, Civil Defence and disaster management has been placed under the State Disaster Management Fund (SDMF). Compared to Simhastha 2016, the proposed deployment of Home Guards will increase from 8,000 to 11,500, while the number of Civil Defence volunteers is proposed to rise from 4,000 to 10,000. Roads, Parking and Transport Arrangements The Public Works Department has proposed several infrastructure works, including levelling of the Mela area at a cost of Rs. 20.51 crore, construction of 122 km of temporary roads for Rs. 34.82 crore, development of 17 km of temporary pathways to the ghats for Rs. 32.34 crore, and development of parking and service areas at a cost of Rs. 112.34 crore. A proposal worth Rs. 19.66 crore has been submitted for widening the 950-metre stretch from Jaisinghpura Tiraha to Narsingh Ghat Bridge. A proposal worth Rs. 17.80 crore had earlier been recommended for the Kartik Chowk–Bada Pul road. However, following the decision to develop it as a six-metre-high integrated submersible bridge over Dani Gate road, the revised proposal, with an estimated cost of Rs. 48.85 crore, has been submitted for approval. This will separate the routes for devotees travelling to and returning from Ram Ghat, making crowd management easier during the major bathing days. The Ujjain Development Authority has proposed Rs. 45 crore for operating 2,000 buses during the Mela, connecting ghats, akharas, parking areas and transport hubs. A signage system worth Rs. 16.80 crore has also been proposed to guide devotees across the Mela area and ghats, of which Rs. 14.80 crore will be mobilised through CSR funds. Administrative Arrangements, Training and Accommodation An allocation of Rs. 120.38 crore has been proposed for administrative tent facilities, including zonal offices, sector offices, sub-offices and dormitories, with a combined accommodation capacity of 40,000 people. Other tent facilities across the city will be developed under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model. The Mela Authority has proposed Rs. 25.15 crore for training officials, employees, vendors, hotel staff and auto-rickshaw drivers. An additional Rs. 10 crore has been proposed for coordination and engagement with saints and seers, as well as for organising related events. A proposal worth Rs. 19.90 crore has also been submitted for constructing a Judges' Guest House, Drivers' Rest House and Seva Bhawan in Ujjain. City Beautification and Simhastha Experience Centre A proposal worth Rs. 100 crore has been submitted for upgrading 147 city junctions, landscaping and place-making at 27 locations. A permanent dome-shaped shed will be constructed in front of Bharat Vishal Rangmanch at the Kalidas Academy complex at a cost of Rs. 11.18 crore. This will eliminate the recurring expenditure on temporary dome structures every year. A major attraction will be the proposed ‘Simhastha Experience Centre’, to be developed over approximately 75,000 square feet under the PPP model at an estimated cost of Rs. 90 crore. Using technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, holograms and projection mapping, the centre will feature 10 thematic zones showcasing Mahakaleshwar, Samudra Manthan, the Kshipra River, the traditions of akharas, Sandipani Ashram and Samrat Vikramaditya, among other themes. The centre will continue to serve as a permanent tourist attraction in Ujjain even after Simhastha. State-of-the-Art Security Arrangements The Home Department (Police) has proposed the procurement of security equipment and vehicles worth a total of Rs. 1,862.67 crore for Simhastha. The proposals include Rs. 207.61 crore for Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS) equipment, Rs. 207.33 crore for security equipment, Rs. 22.92 crore for Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) equipment, Rs. 5.41 crore for cyber-security equipment, Rs. 220.06 crore for traffic and crowd management equipment, and Rs. 199.34 crore for vehicles. Around 100 BDDS teams will be required during Simhastha. Drone-based surveillance and anti-drone technology will also be deployed to strengthen security in Ujjain, Omkareshwar, Maheshwar, other major religious destinations and along interstate borders. Devotee-Centric Arrangements for Simhastha 2028 All these proposed works aim to make Simhastha 2028 a safe, clean, well-organised and devotee-centric event. Special attention has been given to the convenience of senior citizens, women and devotees travelling from distant parking areas. Several initiatives, including city beautification, river rejuvenation, permanent dome structures and the Simhastha Experience Centre, will also become lasting assets for Ujjain beyond the Simhastha celebrations. Pratima Bagri, Chief Secretary Shri Ashok Barnwal, Additional Chief Secretary to the Chief Minister's Office Shri Neeraj Mandloi, Additional Chief Secretaries Shri Sanjay Dubey, Shri Manish Rastogi, Shri Sanjay Kumar Shukla and Shri Shiv Shekhar Shukla, Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister's Office Shri Sukhbir Singh, other Principal Secretaries and Secretaries, and senior administrative officers from Ujjain Division and district were present at the meeting.

articles.title: Keeping watch on diet soda: Why it will never be as good as water
articles.summary: Some people may feel completely fine after consuming diet soda on multiple days of a week, experts have observed. According to a LocalCircles’ survey (2023), one in three of those consuming artificial sweeteners do so in the form of diet soda or sugar free gums. While diet soda emerged as a healthier alternative to sugary drinks, it is yet to be made certain if it is as harmless as plain water. Most of the research on diet soda so far has been very conflicting. While some studies have linked it with weight loss, others have associated it with metabolic impairment over time. Healthline suggested that industry funding could also influence results, enabling its popularity among consumers. WHO's cancer research agency to declare artificial sweetener used in Diet Coke a possible carcinogen What is diet soda? According to experts, a diet soda is a mixture of carbonated water, artificial sweeteners, acids and some flavors. To make them a healthier version of the existing carbonated drinks, sugar gets replaced by artificial sweeteners like aspartame, saccharin, sucralose and others. However, at its core, diet soda still constitutes an ultra processed beverage, experts have warned, involving a multilayered manufacture. The added color and flavor does not make it a health neutral drink, studies suggest, though it has not been evidently proven. Conflicting studies A controlled clinical trial of beverages and weight loss found that consumption of diet soda was linked to slightly greater weight loss among people compared to other beverages. As per some experts, diet soda itself has no active ingredients that can initiate weight loss but it may prevent people from consuming other drinks which are high on sugar. On the contrary, some studies have questioned the ill effects of diet soda on the microbiome of the gut, assuming its daily use can disrupt natural bacterial density, change activity of hunger hormones, making one eat more or develop dependency on these diet drinks . Additionally, its acidic nature also poses risk to enamel health, experts have warned about its effects on dental health. However, many experimental studies have not been able to establish a direct, causative link between diet soda and weight gain and other metabolic disorders. Some literature has indirectly linked it to some cancers of the gastrointestinal tract. There is evidence of bias in scientific literature, Healthline has said, suggesting consumers may be overestimating the benefits associated with these sodas. However, some health experts suggest that adoption of diet soda has been useful to prediabetics or diabetics who find it hard to keep their hands off sugary drinks. Hence, the literature on diet soda is confusing and inconclusive. How to lower intake of diet soda? According to Medical News Today, the following are some ways in which people can lower their dependency on diet sodas: Keeping attractive water bottles that tempts one to drink more water. Try finding ways to make water more attractive to drink, including lemon, herbs, fruits and other things. Try associating routine activities with drinking water, making it a habit. Try to develop new taste experiences.

articles.title: 'My grief has not lost its intensity': Hema Malini pens emotional note on Dharmendra's first death anniversary
articles.summary: It's been a year since the demise of veteran actor Dharmendra, and his wife and actor Hema Malini's "grief has not lost its intensity". Remembering the legendary actor, Malini took to Instagram and shared several never-seen-before pictures with Dharmendra, along with a heartfelt and emotional caption. "A whole year has sped by but my grief has not lost its intensity I grieve over the tremendous and irreparable loss of a man who was not just my husband - he was my everything - my friend, philosopher and guide who was my backbone and in short, was my very existence," she wrote. The 78-year-old actor continued, "Life seems so empty without him. His towering personality, his innate goodness that pervaded his whole being and spread his love towards all who knew him - such a unique human being who, though he reached the pinnacle of success, remained grounded and attached to his roots." View this post on Instagram The Sholay star further shared how she continues to miss Dharmendra's presence. "The Bhagwad Gita tells us the soul is immortal and will be reborn. I am aware of this, but I am still here in this life, and I cannot but miss his loving presence," she added. Thanking the fans for remembering the late legendary actor, Malini concluded, "I thank all the millions of fans who have recalled this generous, lovely human being and sent such warm notes about Dharam ji and what he meant to them. The Amarnath Cave, Yatra and surrounding mountains must be protected as one ecological whole. — Mehbooba Mufti (@MehboobaMufti) November 24, 2026 Situated at an altitude of around 3,590 metres, Sheshnag is an important overnight halt on the traditional Pahalgam route to the Amarnath cave shrine. According to Hindu religious tradition, Lord Shiva left behind the serpents at Sheshnag before proceeding towards the cave to narrate the Amar Katha to Goddess Parvati. articles.title: 'Must protect witness': Kerala HC grants bail to Sri Lankan alleged of LTTE revival case
articles.summary: Kochi: The Kerala High Court has granted bail to a Sri Lankan national allegedly residing in India illegally and accused of having a significant role in a "transnational conspiracy" to finance and facilitate the revival of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) through violent and unlawful means. A bench of justices Raja Vijayaraghavan V and K V Jayakumar said that continued detention of the Sri Lankan national -- Muhammed Asmin -- cannot be justified as he has been given pardon by the special NIA court and he has agreed to assist the prosecution as an approver. "Taking into account the period of incarceration already undergone, the grant of pardon, the fact that some of the co-accused have been enlarged on bail in connected cases and the legal position discussed, we are of the view the appellant (Asmin) is entitled to be released on bail, subject to appropriate conditions to ensure his availability for the proceedings, protect the integrity of the prosecution and safeguard the interests of justice," the bench said. While granting the relief, the High Court also said that the present case was one where the appellant should be considered for protection under the Kerala Witness Protection Scheme. "Accordingly, the Secretary to Government, Home Department, shall take immediate steps to ensure the appellant is brought within the protective framework of the applicable Kerala Witness Protection Scheme and that such protection as may be considered necessary is extended to him in accordance with the provisions of the Scheme," it said. Kerala High Court says Guruvayur temple staff must treat devotees with respect, maintain calm The High Court emphasised that the criminal justice system can function effectively only when persons who come forward to assist the administration of justice, often at considerable personal risk, are assured that their safety will not be compromised on account of their willingness to testify. It said that the protection of witnesses was not merely a matter of individual security and was an essential prerequisite for the fair and effective administration of criminal justice. "A system which expects witnesses to come forward and assist in the prosecution of offenders must also ensure that they are not left vulnerable to threats, intimidation or retaliation," it added. The bench directed Asmin to execute a bond of Rs 1 lakh and furnish two solvent sureties each of the like sum subject to the satisfaction of the special court, surrender his passport and furnish his complete residential address along with his current mobile phone number to the investigating officer of the National Investigation Agency (NIA). "He shall remain within the territorial limits of Ernakulam District and shall not leave the said limits without obtaining the prior permission of the Special Court. He shall also ensure that he is readily available for interrogation or any other lawful requirement of the investigation or trial, whenever called upon by the investigating officer," it directed. The High Court also made it clear that grant of bail to Asmin shall not confer upon him any right to remain in India, nor shall it operate as a bar to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) or any other competent authority from initiating or continuing proceedings in accordance with law under the applicable Laws relating to foreigners. "The competent authorities shall remain at liberty to take such lawful measures as may be warranted concerning his immigration status, including the regulation or restriction of his movement and the requirement to reside at a place designated by such authority," it said. The appellant has also been directed to appear before the investigating or designated officer of the NIA at Ernakulam on every Saturday between 10 am and 11 am until further orders. He was also directed not to communicate with or establish any form of contact with any of the other accused in the case or attempt to influence, intimidate, induce, threaten or otherwise interfere with any prosecution witness. Besides these, the appellant was also directed not to hold any press conference or interaction with the media or make any form of public statement regarding anything related to the case. The conspirators are alleged to have joined hands with international criminal syndicates operating across Pakistan, Sri Lanka and India, with the common objective of financing and facilitating the revival of the LTTE through violent and unlawful means. The NIA told the High Court that through a series of clandestine meetings held at beachfront properties in Chennai and within detention facilities in Trichy, the conspirators devised an elaborate plan to channel large quantities of illicit narcotic substances and sophisticated weaponry into the region. The alleged conspiracy eventually came to light following the interception and seizure of substantial quantities of contraband, including more than 300 kilograms of heroin, AK-56 assault rifles and 1,000 rounds of live ammunition," the bench noted. According to NIA, Asmin was allegedly involved in facilitating the movement of drug consignments, handling proceeds of unlawful transactions through hawala channels and converting the proceeds of crime into cryptocurrency, to finance terrorist activities.

Pakistani pilot Zeeshan Ali to become first foreigner to fly to China's space station
articles.summary: Jiuquan: When the Shenzhou-24 space flight takes off on Wednesday for China's Tiangong space station, it will be a moment of pride not just for China, but also for Pakistan . Zeeshan Ali, a 40-year-old pilot, is set to be the first Pakistani in orbit and the first foreign national to board the space station, as China makes new strides in space diplomacy. Part of a three-man crew that includes Chinese commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi, Ali will work as a payload specialist and is set to stay at the station for 5 to 10 days, conducting experiments. The launch of the spacecraft, which will use a Long March-2F rocket, is scheduled for 8:18 a.m. (0018 GMT) from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. To prepare for the flight, Ali trained for seven months in Beijing, during which he underwent intensive Chinese-language classes, learning Chinese songs and reading Chinese poetry. He also practised calligraphy and played table tennis. "I'm not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder," Ali told reporters. Pakistani astronauts to fly aboard China’s space station soon: Senior Chinese astronaut Space cooperation between China and Pakistan dates back to the early 1990s. China has launched Pakistani satellites and a Pakistani-built rover is also set to fly on a Chinese lunar mission around 2028. "China has always been very good at using space for soft power outreach," said Victoria Samson, chief director of US-based Space Security and Stability at the Secure World Foundation. "See how many satellites it builds and launches for other countries, and how it builds telescopes and tracking centres in the Global South — so this is just one more action of that same genre," she said. A long stay for one Chinese astronaut While Ali's stay is much shorter than the usual six-month rotation for a Chinese astronaut, it is a big deal for Pakistan. "It brings prestige, important science and technology know-how, and a level of deeper collaboration and diplomatic goodwill with China," said Blaine Curcio, ​founder of Hong Kong-based Orbital Gateway Consulting. The mission underscores Beijing's vision to promote its Tiangong space station as a hub for international space cooperation as the NASA-led International Space Station (ISS) faces possible retirement by 2030. "By having an international astronaut, China is making it clear that they are open for business," Curcio said. China's self-built station, named Tiangong or Celestial Palace in Chinese, has been fully operational since late 2022. It can host up to six astronauts during handovers when an arriving three-person crew overlaps with the departing crew. This time, the handover will be different. Shenzhou-23 commander Zhu Yangzhu will stay on to support Beijing's study of how the human body copes in space — a crucial step towards a planned crewed mission to the moon and a potential journey to Mars. The rest of the Shenzhou-23 crew departs Tiangong alongside Ali. Zhu, who will stay for a year, will hold the record for the longest single stay in orbit by a Chinese astronaut by the time he leaves, though that will fall short of the 14-1/2-month record set by a Russian cosmonaut in 1995. China's goal of human presence on the moon by 2030 remains unchanged following the postponement of its Chang'e-7 lunar mission, which was delayed this year after failing to meet launch conditions amid adverse weather linked to a tropical storm. Beijing rejects such allegations, saying it advocates peaceful use of outer space. Flying to the moon was also on Ali's mind. "I hope for the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation to grow from one astronaut, one flight to multiple joint flights, to (the) moon, Mars and beyond," he said.

articles.title: Pancreatic cancer pill: Here's why it's a ‘massive breakthrough’ in medicine
articles.summary: With an extremely poor prognosis in advanced stages, diagnosis of pancreatic cancer is not easily digestible for both doctors and patients alike. This dreaded form of cancer can carry a mortality rate as high as 98 per cent with a maximum survival span of five years, the American Cancer Society has stated. However, most people die between three to eight months after getting a diagnosis, experts have said, with only a small 3 per cent living over a year. When some scientists at Revolution Medicines had presented trial (III) findings at the annual meeting of American Society of Clinical Oncology 2026 (May) earlier this year, the medical community had hailed the drug Daraxonrasib (to be branded as Rasonque) as a potential breakthrough in this undruggable form of illness. The latest clinical trial findings (trial I/II) showed that one in 12 people who had been given daraxonrasib along with chemotherapy, the cancer had become undetectable on imaging scans. The daily pill was able to stop tumors from growing in almost 61 participants who were recently diagnosed with pancreatic cancer, and in whom the cancer cells had spread to other parts of the body. While the results look very promising, the researchers are still figuring out if the pill can be a cure for the illness and how for how long it can keep cancer growth at bay. Nonetheless, the medicine has given a massive hope to people battling the disease. Reproductive cancer burden highest among women aged 40-59: Study Optimistic findings Medical doctors across the world have not hesitated calling it the ‘biggest leap’ when it comes to treating aggressive pancreatic cancer . The phase III of the clinical trials on the efficacy of Daraxonrasib had involved cancer patients who had metastasis (cancer had spread to other parts of the body) and had already tried out conventional treatments like chemotherapy. It was found to nearly double the median survival period for these patients from 6.6 months to 13.2 months. The findings had won approval of the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) this year. The latest findings which were presented at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium 2026 on molecular targets and cancer therapeutics (in Barcelona, Spain) around November 20, listed some optimistic developments. This time, the daily pill was used as first line treatment alongside chemotherapy. The results showed that tumors stopped growing in 90 per cent of the patients, in around 60 per cent of the patients, the tumors were shrinking or disappearing and around 8 per cent of the patients, cancerous growth became undetectable on scans. Longer survival As per medical experts, a cancerous growth in, on and around the pancreas is notoriously difficult to spot during the early stages, partly because of its anatomically cushioned position and also because of absence of loud symptoms. Most people get diagnosed in later stages of the illness, informed experts. Due to its ‘crushable’ texture and the organ seated deep inside the abdomen with major blood vessels around it, surgical removal of the cancerous growth becomes risky. Even if one goes for partial surgery, it involves restructuring of the abdomen through another complicated procedure, increasing mortality risks. Hence, chemotherapy is the most potent treatment option which can shrink the tumor. Chemotherapy, however, poses the risk of treatment toxicity and many people are not able to follow through it. Also, the tumor can still regrow after standard chemotherapy sessions end. According to experts, the risk of regrowth has not been cleared out with the new pill but it can allow the patient to live a little longer with lesser side effects. Targeting KRAS genes The KRAS protein technically acts like an ‘on-off switch’ which controls cell growth. If there are unpleasant mutations in the KRAS gene, it can cause the RAS protein to consistently stay in the ‘on’ mode, causing uncontrolled cell growth. Many forms of pancreatic cancer are driven by mutations in the KRAS genes. The medicine, Daraxonrasib, has been designed to target the mutated KRAS genes, bind to the proteins and influence their behavior. It will turn off mutations that cause tumor growth, experts have said. Aiming for remission While doctors are not certain that the daily pill can put pancreatic cancer in remission, a state where detectable signs and symptoms of cancer disappear, it has been found to shrink or even vanish tumors in a percentage of patients. As per an expert talking to the Guardian, if the median follow up for the treatment was 18 months and the cancer cells did not grow back, it was a sign close to remission. However, more evidence will be needed to confirm if it can be a cure to this life threatening illness. For the largest section of the medical community, this medicine has been the greatest breakthrough in this area so far.

articles.title: Journey of SAD-BJP alliance | From 'nail and flesh bond' to rupture and then reunion
articles.summary: New Delhi: For years, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) patriarch Parkash Singh Badal described his party's relationship with the BJP as "nau-maas da rishta" (the bond between the nail and the flesh), projecting the alliance as much as a guarantor of communal harmony in Punjab. The partnership, which saw the two parties govern Punjab for 15 years across three five-year terms, came apart in September 2020 when the Akalis walked out of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over the Centre's three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed. On Tuesday, as the two parties announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls, SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal invoked his late father's description of the relationship at a joint press conference with Union Home Minister Amit Shah and BJP national president Nitin Nabin at the BJP headquarters here. Punjab BJP forms state election committee for 2027 Assembly polls Shah welcomed the return of the NDA's "oldest ally", while Nabin described the partnership as a "natural alliance". The announcement, coinciding with the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, capped months of negotiations between the two parties, which have suffered successive electoral setbacks in Punjab after parting ways. The association predates the formation of the BJP in 1980. Its predecessor, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, was part of coalition governments with the Akalis in 1967 and 1969 following Punjab's reorganisation. The partnership in its modern form took shape in 1996, when the SAD, through its Moga Declaration, sought to broaden its appeal beyond its traditional Panthic constituency by embracing the idea of "Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat". Coming in the aftermath of militancy in Punjab, the alliance brought together the predominantly rural Sikh constituency of the Akalis and the BJP's largely urban Hindu support base. Under their longstanding seat-sharing arrangement, the SAD contested 94 of the 117 assembly seats, leaving 23 for the BJP. In Lok Sabha polls, the corresponding figures were 10 and three. The alliance won 93 seats in the 1997 assembly polls -- the SAD bagging 75 and the BJP 18. After losing power to the Congress in 2002, the combine returned to office in 2007 with 68 seats and retained power in 2012 with an identical tally, bucking Punjab's trend of voting out incumbent governments. However, the emergence of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), coupled with public anger over incidents of sacrilege and the drug menace, reduced the SAD to 15 seats and the BJP to three in 2017. Three years later, the farmers' agitation against the Centre's agricultural reform measures brought differences between the two parties to a head. On September 17, 2020, Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned as Union food processing industries minister. Nine days later, the SAD snapped its 24-year-old electoral partnership with the BJP. 'NDA’s oldest ally is returning': BJP, Akali Dal join hands for 2027 Punjab elections six years after parting ways Sukhbir Badal linked the deterioration in ties to the BJP's growing numerical strength in Parliament, accusing it of not taking allies into confidence on major policy decisions. In subsequent years, the Akalis accused the BJP of interfering in Sikh religious affairs, even as several senior SAD leaders crossed over to the saffron party. The BJP, meanwhile, sought to shed its image as the junior partner, with its leaders arguing that the alliance had restricted its organisational expansion in rural Punjab. The repeal of the farm laws in November 2021 did not immediately pave the way for a rapprochement, but electoral compulsions made it inevitable after a point. In the 2022 assembly polls, the SAD, contesting in alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), won just three seats, with its vote share falling from 25.24 per cent in 2017 to 18.38 per cent. The BJP, which tied up with Amarinder Singh's Punjab Lok Congress and Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa-led SAD (Sanyukt), won two seats. The AAP swept Punjab, winning 92 seats. Efforts to revive the alliance ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls failed amid renewed farmers' protests. In 2019, the SAD and the BJP had won two Lok Sabha seats each, polling a combined 37.08 per cent of the votes. Five years later, the BJP's vote share rose from 9.63 per cent to 18.56 per cent as it contested all 13 seats, while the SAD's fell from 27.45 per cent to 13.42 per cent. The BJP drew a blank, while the SAD retained Bathinda. Their combined vote share of nearly 32 per cent was, however, higher than that of either the Congress or the AAP. This strengthened the proponents of reviving the alliance. The signals became more pronounced this year. On August 7, Sukhbir Badal called on Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Parliament House, fuelling speculation over a reunion. Harsimrat Kaur Badal, whose resignation had set the separation in motion, publicly recalled the developmental benefits of the alliance. Her brother and senior SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia also advocated a reunion. Punjab Assembly elections 2027: Six years after split, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance In October, Shah predicted that an NDA government would assume office in Punjab in 2027, reiterating it in Chandigarh on November 1. Asked about an alliance on November 2, Badal said, "You will come to know in a few days as to what will happen." While the BJP has spent the last six years making efforts to expand its organisational footprint in Punjab, the SAD is fighting to reclaim lost political ground.

articles.title: Over Rs. 7,000 Cr Approved for Overall Development, Infrastructure Expansion and Public Welfare in MP
articles.summary: Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav chaired a Cabinet meeting held at the Mantralaya on Monday. Minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Shri Chaitanya Kumar Kashyap briefed the media on the Cabinet decisions. He informed that the Cabinet had approved more than Rs. 7,000 crore for the overall development of the state, expansion of infrastructure and public welfare. The Cabinet ratified the implementation of the Gopal-Krishna Gram Puraskar Yojana to promote milk production and improved indigenous cattle breeds in the state. It also approved Rs. 325 crore as share capital assistance to strengthen the financial position of nine financially weak District Cooperative Central Banks. In addition, the tenure of overdue elections to Multipurpose Primary Agricultural Credit Cooperative Societies was extended by one year. The Cabinet also approved a Rs. 193.72 crore action plan under the first phase of the Government of India's Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) for electrification of more than 46,000 unelectrified households in 1,834 habitations and 54 government public institutions across the state. Approval was also granted to appoint the Madhya Pradesh State Mining Corporation Limited as the implementing agency for the implementation of the State Mineral Exploration Policy. Under the establishment of Vedanta Peeth, the Cabinet approved Rs. 2,278.99 crore for the construction of ‘Advaita Lok’ at Ekatm Dham in Omkareshwar for the period of the 16th Finance Commission, covering the financial years 2026-27 to 2030-31. For the same period, Rs. 3,059.07 crore was approved for the continuation of 23 schemes of the General Administration Department. The Cabinet also sanctioned Rs. 1,165 crore for the continuation of the scheme related to the Chief Minister's Discretionary Grant. Gopal-Krishna Gram Puraskar Yojana Approved to Promote Milk Production and Indigenous Cattle Breeds The Cabinet ratified the implementation of the Gopal-Krishna Gram Puraskar Yojana under the Animal Husbandry and Dairy Department. One of the nine components of the Mukhyamantri Pashupalan Vikas Yojana, namely the award scheme for indigenous cattle breeds of the state and improved Indian milch cows, has been discontinued and replaced with this new scheme. In compliance with the announcement made by the Chief Minister on October 3, 2026, the Cabinet ratified the departmental order issued on October 26, 2026. The primary objective of the scheme is to more than double milk production in the state, establish Madhya Pradesh as the country's ‘Milk Capital’, increase the income of cattle rearers and conserve and promote improved indigenous milch cattle breeds such as Gir, Sahiwal, Tharparkar and Malvi. In the first year of implementation, 2026-27, competitions will be organised among cattle rearers in one identified ‘Vrindavan Gram’ in each of the state's 208 rural Assembly constituencies. From 2027-28 to 2030-31, the competition will be organised at the block level across all 313 development blocks of the state. Cattle rearers belonging to all sections of society will be eligible to participate, provided they own a milch cow of an improved indigenous Indian breed producing at least six litres of milk per day. Winners will be selected through a transparent process by block-level and district-level committees on the basis of the average milk yield recorded during three milking sessions. Awards will be distributed every year on the occasion of Govardhan Puja. In each Vrindavan Gram and development block, cattle rearers owning the highest milk-yielding cows will receive a first prize of Rs. 1 lakh, a second prize of Rs. 50,000 and a third prize of Rs. 25,000. The entire prize amount awarded to the winning cattle rearers will be utilised exclusively for the purchase, conservation and promotion of indigenous cattle breeds. Rs. 325 Crore Approved as Share Capital Assistance to District Cooperative Central Banks The Cabinet has approved Rs. 325 crore as share capital assistance to improve the financial position of nine financially weak District Cooperative Central Banks in the state. Five weak District Cooperative Central Banks in Rewa, Satna, Datia, Shivpuri and Jabalpur will receive share capital assistance of Rs. 25 crore each during the financial year 2026-27. The Cabinet has also decided to strengthen the financial position of four other weak District Cooperative Central Banks. Under this provision, the district banks in Raisen, Morena, Sagar and Sidhi will receive share capital assistance of Rs. 50 crore each during the current financial year 2026-27. Tenure of Elections to Multipurpose Primary Agricultural Credit Cooperative Societies Extended by One Year The Cabinet has decided to extend the tenure of overdue elections to Multipurpose Primary Agricultural Credit Cooperative Societies in the state by one year. The process of reorganising these societies in previously uncovered Gram Panchayats is currently underway, and operations have not yet commenced in all newly constituted societies. Conducting elections before these societies become operational could lead to legal and operational difficulties in the future. In view of these special circumstances, the decision to extend the election period has been taken. The Cabinet has also decided to extend the tenure of elections to marketing societies, District Cooperative Banks and other cooperative institutions, wherever necessary. This will ensure the participation of elected representatives of Multipurpose Primary Agricultural Credit Cooperative Societies in these elections. The Cooperation Department has been authorised to undertake the necessary proceedings for extending the election period of these societies and District Cooperative Banks in accordance with the provisions of the Cooperative Societies Act. Rs. 193.72 Crore Approved to Electrify Over 46,000 Households in the State The Cabinet has approved an action plan for the electrification of unelectrified households under the Government of India's Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS). Under the first phase of the scheme, an action plan worth Rs. 193.72 crore has been approved for electrifying 46,574 households in 1,834 habitations across the eastern, central and western regions of the state, along with 54 government public institutions. The approved amount includes a 60 per cent Central Government grant of Rs. 116.24 crore and a 40 per cent state government contribution of Rs. 77.48 crore. As per the decision, electricity distribution companies will develop the required power infrastructure with financial support from the Central and State Governments. The initiative will cover habitations where the estimated electrification cost is up to Rs. 2 lakh per household. The remaining project cost, excluding the Central Government grant, along with the SGST payable on the Central Government's share, will be provided by the State Government to the distribution companies in the form of a loan. In-principle approval has also been granted for providing financial assistance from the State Government for electrifying habitations with fewer than 20 households. A separate proposal for this purpose will be submitted. The Energy Department has been authorised to make necessary amendments or modifications to the scheme guidelines. State Mineral Corporation Approved as Implementing Agency for Mineral Exploration Policy The Cabinet has approved the appointment of Madhya Pradesh State Mining Corporation Limited as the nodal agency for mineral exploration and survey activities in the state. The responsibility for the smooth execution and supervision of these activities has also been entrusted to the Corporation's Board of Directors. Under the approved proposal, external agencies will be appointed through a transparent process for various activities, including analysis of available data, analysis of high-altitude airborne survey data, followed by low-altitude heli-borne surveys, geophysical and geochemical surveys in identified high-potential areas, and drilling to establish mineral reserves. All such appointments will be made through Madhya Pradesh State Mining Corporation Limited. In addition, survey work in Category-III areas located in the central and western parts of the state will be completed by the end of 2028, based on the analysis of data from three baseline surveys. Rs. 3,059.07 Crore Approved for Continuation of 23 General Administration Department Schemes The Cabinet has approved a total allocation of Rs. 3,059.07 crore for the continuation of 23 ongoing schemes of the General Administration Department during the 16th Finance Commission period, covering the financial years 2026-27 to 2030-31. The approval includes major schemes relating to Secretariat administration, Loktantra Senani Samman Nidhi, pensions for freedom fighters, grants-in-aid to the Human Rights Commission, the Quality Assurance Council and the Chief Minister's Excellence Awards. Financial provisions have also been made for ministers' salaries, assistance and discretionary grants, honorariums and allowances for former Chief Ministers, information technology-related activities, construction of an annexe in the Chief Minister's residential complex and other administrative requirements. Rs. 1,165 Crore Approved for Chief Minister's Discretionary Grant Scheme The Cabinet has approved Rs. 1,165 crore for the continuation of the scheme related to the Chief Minister's Discretionary Grant under the General Administration Department during the 16th Finance Commission period, from the financial year 2026-27 to 2030-31. Rs. 2,278.99 Crore Approved for Construction of ‘Advaita Lok’ at Ekatm Dham The Cabinet has approved Rs. 2,278.99 crore for the construction of ‘Advaita Lok’ at Ekatm Dham, being developed in Omkareshwar under the initiative for the establishment of Vedanta Peeth. The allocation will cover the 16th Finance Commission period from 2026-27 to 2030-31. ‘Advaita Lok’ (Shankar Museum) at Ekatm Dham will showcase the life, contributions and philosophy of Advaita Vedanta of Acharya Shankar to visitors, tourists and devotees through various attractions and facilities. These will include a high-screen theatre, Maya Gallery, laser light, water and sound show, Advaita Narmada Vihar, Nididhyasan Centre, art gallery, Shankar Stambh, Annapurna, Kalagram and Panchayatan Temple, among others.
